hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y with positive gain (heater warms sensor).
Response has first-order lag of tens of seconds; settling takes several times the initial lag, so a 180s hold may not fully settle.
There is no large dead zone: u=0.5 clearly produces a rise above ambient.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 due to heat loss to room.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u in [0,1].
Steady-state u needed to hold target y=0.5 is in mid-range approx 0.2-0.8.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) relative to control band width 0.05.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Gain magnitude and lag/settling time at a safe mid power; distinguishes fast-small-gain vs slow-large-gain and gives first steady-state estimate for target 0.5.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is 0.0508 + 0.006*0.5*180 = 0.5908, which stays 0.259 below soft limit 0.85 assuming no decay or lag.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.05 toward 0.3-0.5 with decreasing slope, staying below 0.6 and showing non-zero end slope if not yet settled.
proposal.readiness_justification: No experiments completed yet, so gain magnitude, lag, u=0 decay rate, linearity, steady-state u for 0.5, and noise are all unresolved; at least 3 experiments including a second amplitude and a u=0 decay are needed before controller design.
proposal.operator_note: First heating test at half power for 180s to measure warming rate, lag and approximate gain.

Positive gain, no large deadzone, and low noise are partly resolved, but steady-state value at u=0.5, cooling rate at u=0, and linearity across amplitudes remain unmeasured and are all needed for controller design.
proposal.operator_note: Continuing 0.5 power hold to watch temperature settle toward its equilibrium.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Linearity of steady-state gain and steady-state input for target: a second amplitude (u=0.6) from current low y discriminates linear vs saturating gain and refines feedforward for y=0.5.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.1905 + 0.006*0.6*180 = 0.8385 stays below soft limit 0.85; true physics includes passive loss and lag so actual y ~0.48 will be far lower.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order heater with tau ~120-150s and ambient ~0.05 is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.19 toward ~0.58 inf, reaching ~0.45-0.50 after 180s with end slope ~0.0007-0.001/s still positive, staying below 0.6. A much smaller rise would indicate sub-linear gain or dead-zone; a much larger/faster rise would indicate super-linear gain.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, passive decay, lag/tau, noise, and u~0.5 for target are resolved by E1-E3, but linearity across u is unresolved with only one non-zero level tested, so a controller gain cannot yet be trusted; one bounded second-amplitude hold is needed before generating.
proposal.operator_note: E3 confirmed passive cooling; next heating at 0.6 from low temperature tests gain linearity.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y with positive gain (heater warms sensor).
Response has first-order lag with tau ~120-160s; settling takes ~300-400s, so a 180s hold alone may not fully settle.
There is no large dead zone: u=0.5 and u=0.6 clearly produce rise from low y.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 due to heat loss to room.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u in [0,1]; u=0.6 drives to higher ss than u=0.5.
Steady-state u needed to hold target y=0.5 is ~0.51-0.53; u=0.5 holds ~0.491 (inside band low edge) and u=0.6 drives through 0.5 with positive slope to ss>0.5.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) relative to control band width 0.05; quantization step ~0.005.
Initial response delay is short (<15s); rise begins within ~10s of step, then slow exponential approach.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input to hold y=0.5 and local gain around target; distinguishes u=0.5 holds band vs needs higher feedforward, which sets controller bias.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.502+0.006*0.5*100=0.802 stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin; true rise will be far smaller due to heat loss and because start is near equilibrium.
proposal.expected_observation: If u=0.5 steady state ~0.49 hypothesis is right, y starting ~0.502 will stay flat or decay very slightly to ~0.49-0.50 with end slope near 0 (+/-0.0003), remaining inside band 0.475-0.525. Continued rise would imply ss>0.51.
proposal.readiness_justification: Gain direction, decay at zero, lag order, and noise are resolved enough for control, but feedforward for target is not: E2 showed u=0.5 settles ~0.491 from below while E4 left y=0.502 rising at 0.0012/s under u=0.6, so holding behavior from above is untested. One bounded hold at u=0.5 is needed before a controller can be justified.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping down to u=0.5 for 100s to verify it holds temperature in band.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y with positive gain (heater warms sensor).
Response has first-order lag with tau ~200-300s; settling takes ~400-600s, so 140-180s holds do not fully settle and flat slope over 5s can be quantization artifact.
There is no large dead zone: u=0.5 and u=0.6 clearly produce rise from low y, and u=0.5 produces rise from ~0.50.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 due to heat loss to room.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u in [0,1]; u=0.6 drives to higher ss than u=0.5, but absolute ss values not yet settled.
Prior estimate that u=0.5 holds ~0.491 is falsified by E5: ss for u=0.5 is >0.534 (rose 0.502 to 0.534 in 100s); steady-state u to hold y=0.5 is <0.5, likely 0.40-0.48.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) relative to control band width 0.05; quantization step ~0.005 with multi-sample plateaus causing zero 5s slope even while trending.
Initial response delay is short (<15s); rise begins within ~6-12s of step, then slow exponential approach.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input to hold y=0.5 after E5 falsification; a step down to u=0.4 from above band discriminates whether ss(0.4) is near 0.5 versus still above, directly setting feedforward bias for control.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.5343 + 0.006*0.4*120 = 0.8223 stays below soft limit 0.85 with no decay or lag credited.
proposal.expected_observation: Starting ~0.534 under u=0.4, y will flatten then decay slowly toward band if ss(u=0.5)>0.534 hypothesis is right, reaching ~0.51-0.53 after 120s with small negative end slope and staying below 0.6. Continued rise would imply ss(u=0.4)>0.534 and even lower feedforward needed.
proposal.readiness_justification: Have 5 completed experiments. Direction, decay at zero, short delay, and small noise are resolved. Steady-state input for target is NOT resolved because E5 contradicted E2 apparent settling, and tau/gain magnitude remain uncertain by ~20-30%, so a controller bias cannot be set reliably yet; one lower-u hold near target is needed and affordable with 3 experiments left.
proposal.operator_note: E5 falsified u=0.5 settling at 0.49 by rising to 0.534, so next step down to 0.4 to find input that holds 0.5.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y with positive gain (heater warms sensor).
Response has first-order lag with tau ~150-200s; settling takes ~600-800s, so 100-180s holds do not fully settle and flat 5s slope can be quantization artifact.
There is no large dead zone: u=0.4-0.6 all produce clear response, including small steps around 0.5.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 due to heat loss to room.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u in [0,1] with gain ~1.0 and ambient ~0.05, i.e. ss(u)~0.05+1.0*u.
Prior estimate that u=0.5 holds ~0.491 is falsified: ss(0.5)>0.534 from E5 rise and ss(0.4)<0.491 from E6 decay with negative end slope, so steady-state u to hold y=0.5 is in (0.4,0.5), likely ~0.45.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) relative to control band width 0.05; quantization step ~0.005 with multi-sample plateaus causing zero 5s slope even while trending.
Initial response delay is short (<15s); rise/decay begins within ~6-20s of step, then slow exponential approach.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.5; distinguishes ss(0.45)~0.5 vs below/above, directly setting controller feedforward bias.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no decay or lag: 0.4913 + 0.006*0.45*120 = 0.815 stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin to hard cutoff 0.9.
proposal.expected_observation: If u*=0.45 holds ~0.5 hypothesis is right, y starting ~0.491 will stay in band 0.475-0.525, flat or drifting slightly up to ~0.49-0.51 with end slope near zero (|slope|<0.0005). Continued decay below 0.48 would imply ss(0.45)<0.49; rise above 0.52 would imply ss(0.45)>0.52.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, self-cooling, short delay, low noise, and long tau are resolved well enough for control, but exact feedforward to hold 0.5 is only bounded to (0.4,0.5) with ~0.04 width, which is comparable to the 0.05 band; one discriminating hold at 0.45 from near-target is needed before a bias plus feedback controller can be justified.
proposal.operator_note: Testing u=0.45 near target to pin feedforward that holds 0.5.

proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.4967+0.006*0.45*120=0.821 stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin, and far below hard cutoff 0.9.

Not yet ready because 300s scored hold needs demonstrated long-horizon stability at u* but only 120s in-band at u=0.45 (E7) has been seen, so one extended same-command hold is needed before designing feedforward+integral controller.
